# SUMMARY

Europe Brent Spot Price FOB (Dollars per Barrel) [https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=rbrte&f=D](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=rbrte&f=D)

Monthly mean prices are modelled with ARIMA and ETS on the log scale and
compared with the random walk (naive) forecast, the usual benchmark for oil
prices (Alquist, Kilian and Vigfusson, 2011), on a 24 month test set and with
rolling origin cross-validation. The ARIMA model selected with all the data
gives the forecast for the next 12 months.


# LOAD DATA

## Load Packages

```{r setup}
library(plotly)
library(forecast)
library(tseries)
library(ggplot2)
source("R/brent.R")
```

## Download and Read Data

The EIA Excel file is downloaded again if the local copy is older than a week.

```{r}
download_brent()
brent_daily <- read_brent()
brent <- monthly_brent(brent_daily)
```

Daily data from `r start(brent_daily)` to `r end(brent_daily)`
(`r nrow(brent_daily)` observations), `r length(brent)` complete months.

```{r}
summary(brent_daily)
```


# EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS

## Daily Prices

```{r}
brent_df <- data.frame(Date = index(brent_daily),
                       USD_Barrel = as.numeric(brent_daily))

plot_ly(data = brent_df,
        x = ~Date,
        y = ~USD_Barrel,
        type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines") %>%
  layout(title = "Europe Brent Spot Price FOB",
         xaxis = list(title = ""),
         yaxis = list(title = "Price (USD/Barrel)")
         )
```

## Prices Histogram

```{r}
plot_ly(data = brent_df,
        x = ~USD_Barrel,
        type = "histogram") %>%
  layout(title = "Daily Prices Histogram",
         xaxis = list(title = "Price (USD/Barrel)")
  )
```

## Monthly Prices

```{r monthly-prices}
autoplot(brent) +
  labs(title = "Brent monthly mean price", x = "", y = "USD/Barrel")
```

## STL Decomposition

Variance grows with the price level, so the decomposition is done on `log(price)`.

```{r stl-decomposition}
autoplot(stl(log(brent), s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE)) +
  labs(title = "STL decomposition of log(price)")
```

The seasonal component is very small compared with the trend and the remainder.


# STATIONARITY

Augmented Dickey-Fuller (H0: unit root) and KPSS (H0: stationary) tests on the
log prices and on the monthly log returns.

```{r}
log_brent <- log(brent)
returns <- diff(log_brent)

stationarity <- function(x) {
  c(ADF_p = adf.test(x)$p.value, KPSS_p = kpss.test(x)$p.value)
}

round(rbind(`log(price)` = stationarity(log_brent),
            `diff(log(price))` = stationarity(returns)), 3)

ndiffs(log_brent)
nsdiffs(log_brent)
```

Log prices have a unit root; one difference makes the series stationary.

```{r log-returns}
autoplot(returns) +
  labs(title = "Monthly log returns", x = "", y = "diff(log(price))")
```

## ACF and PACF of Returns

```{r acf-pacf}
ggtsdisplay(returns, main = "Monthly log returns")
```


# MODELS

## Train and Test Sets

The last 24 months are kept as test set.

```{r}
h_test <- 24
train <- head(brent, length(brent) - h_test)
test <- tail(brent, h_test)
```

## Fit Models

All models are fitted on the log scale (`lambda = 0`) and back-transformed
with bias adjustment.

```{r}
fit_arima <- auto.arima(train, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE,
                        stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
fit_ets <- ets(train, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE)
fit_arima
fit_ets

fc <- list(
  Naive = rwf(train, h = h_test, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE),
  Drift = rwf(train, h = h_test, drift = TRUE, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE),
  ETS = forecast(fit_ets, h = h_test),
  ARIMA = forecast(fit_arima, h = h_test)
)
```

## Test Set Accuracy

```{r}
test_accuracy <- t(sapply(fc, function(f) accuracy(f, test)["Test set", ]))
knitr::kable(test_accuracy[, c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")], digits = 3)
```

```{r test-forecasts}
autoplot(window(brent, start = time(test)[1] - 4)) +
  autolayer(fc$Naive, series = "Naive", PI = FALSE) +
  autolayer(fc$Drift, series = "Drift", PI = FALSE) +
  autolayer(fc$ETS, series = "ETS", PI = FALSE) +
  autolayer(fc$ARIMA, series = "ARIMA", PI = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Forecasts on the test set", x = "", y = "USD/Barrel",
       colour = "Model")
```

## Time Series Cross-Validation

A single test set depends a lot on what happened in those 24 months. Rolling
origin evaluation since 2005 compares ARIMA (with the order chosen above) and
the naive forecast for horizons of 1 to 12 months.

```{r}
h_cv <- 12
order <- arimaorder(fit_arima)
seasonal <- if (length(order) > 3) order[4:6] else c(0, 0, 0)
arima_cv <- function(y, h) {
  forecast(Arima(y, order = order[1:3], seasonal = seasonal,
                 include.drift = "drift" %in% names(coef(fit_arima)),
                 lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE), h = h)
}
naive_cv <- function(y, h) rwf(y, h = h, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE)

initial <- sum(time(brent) < 2005)
e_arima <- tsCV(brent, arima_cv, h = h_cv, initial = initial)
e_naive <- tsCV(brent, naive_cv, h = h_cv, initial = initial)

cv_rmse <- data.frame(
  h = 1:h_cv,
  ARIMA = sqrt(colMeans(e_arima^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Naive = sqrt(colMeans(e_naive^2, na.rm = TRUE))
)
knitr::kable(cv_rmse, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r cv-rmse}
ggplot(cv_rmse, aes(x = h)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ARIMA, colour = "ARIMA")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Naive, colour = "Naive")) +
  labs(title = "Cross-validated RMSE by horizon", x = "Horizon (months)",
       y = "RMSE (USD/Barrel)", colour = "Model")
```


# FORECAST

## Final Model

The ARIMA model is selected again with all the data.

```{r}
fit <- auto.arima(brent, lambda = 0, biasadj = TRUE,
                  stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
fit
```

## Residuals

```{r residuals}
checkresiduals(fit)
```

## Next 12 Months

```{r forecast}
brent_fc <- forecast(fit, h = 12)

autoplot(window(brent, start = end(brent)[1] - 8)) +
  autolayer(brent_fc, series = "ARIMA") +
  labs(title = paste("Brent forecast:", as.character(fit)),
       x = "", y = "USD/Barrel") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

knitr::kable(as.data.frame(brent_fc), digits = 2)
```

The 95 % interval is wide: as with most financial series, the monthly
returns are close to white noise and the point forecast stays near the
last price. Cross-validation shows how much (or how little) ARIMA improves
on the random walk.
